title: Default Interface
concept: The Default interface provides a sensible default value for a type — used by constructors, collections, and configuration patterns.
why: Many patterns need a 'zero value' or 'empty state'. Default standardizes this across all types, enabling generic default construction.
tips: Default should be a SENSIBLE starting point — not just a zeroed struct
Use Default for configuration structs — callers override only what they need
Map::entry().or_default() relies on Default — implement it for values
Default differs per domain: default port is 80 for HTTP but 22 for SSH
common_mistakes: Using zero-valued defaults that violate type invariants — e.g., PositiveInt::default() == 0
Not implementing Default when the type clearly has a sensible default state
Making Default do I/O or allocation — it should be lightweight and infallible
